title: Why Dating Costs So Much Now (Apps Charge You to Stay Single)
alts: Dating Apps Don't Want You to Find Someone. Here's Why.
Why Your $40/Month Dating App Has Zero Matches
line1: Why does your dating app cost $40 a month with zero matches? Because a match that ends your subscription is bad for its business.
summary: Dave pays $40 a month for a dating app and still has zero matches. We break down how dating apps actually make money (Match Group and Bumble's real 2025 revenue, and how one company quietly owns Tinder, Hinge, Match, OkCupid and more), why a happy couple who deletes the app is a lost customer, the FTC's case against Match Group over fake 'someone likes you' emails, what your subscription actually buys (a 'paywall buffet' of removed annoyances), why swiping feels like a slot machine, and how much dates themselves now cost ('date-flation'). Then a light, practical way to date without going broke.
